solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Verbal order declaring immoral levy

indicators.note: declaring means saying out loud, so the phrase is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: an immoral levy is a sin tax, a duty on vices such as drink and tobacco

explanation.surface: A spoken command announces an unethical new charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declaring' asks you to say SIN TAX, which sounds like the word for sentence structure.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the rule-governed arrangement of words in a sentence, a grammatical order.

clue.text: Investor not popular with vampires?

definitions.meaning: someone who has a financial share in a business
read literally, a person holding a wooden ..., the traditional way to kill a vampire

explanation.definitionFit: A person with a share in a venture is an investor; a person gripping a wooden spike is a vampire's nightmare.

clue.text: File clue for a fresh start

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay says a new arrangement of the letters of the word life, which gives this clue word

explanation.surface: A document provides a hint towards beginning again.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as an instruction, makes the clue word. 'clue for' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting a new life means beginning afresh, a clean slate.

clue.text: Kinky and sexual dream of novelist

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the following letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A perverse erotic fantasy belonging to a writer of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' rearranges all fourteen letters of AND SEXUAL DREAM; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandre Dumas wrote The Three Musketeers, so he is a French writer of fiction.

clue.text: See 1 down
Music for liver and kidneys?

definitions.meaning: a concert performance on a pipe instrument
humorously, a long listing of one's bodily ailments, internal parts one by one

explanation.definitionFit: A keyboard concert in a church is musical; jokingly, the phrase also describes a bore reciting their bodily complaints.

clue.text: Early signs of dangerous, erratic and rash tyrannical rulers

indicators.note: the early signs of words are their opening letters, taken from the two words that follow

parts.note: a rash shows on the skin as spots

explanation.surface: The first warnings of reckless, unpredictable behaviour in autocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early signs of' takes only D and E; 'rash' looks like an adjective in the list but is a noun meaning spots, and 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Despots are autocrats who wield absolute and often cruel power.

clue.text: Mother restrained by equipment: part of a long procedure

parts.note: a rig is a set of gear or equipment
ma is an informal word for mother
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A mother held back by machinery takes a role in a drawn-out process.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'part' look like the start of the definition, but it supplies the final piece; 'restrained by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a tedious, complicated sequence of steps, an unnecessarily lengthy process.

clue.text: Why Sean translated 'stop me ere thy cup runneth over'

definitions.text: stop me ere thy cup runneth over

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so these letters are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irishman's words rendered as a biblical-sounding plea not to overfill a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges WHY SEAN; the rest of the clue echoes Psalm 23's cup running over.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosts pouring drinks are told to stop at the right moment with this phrase, a request to halt the pouring.

clue.text: Either way, a middle class story

indicators.note: either way says the letters read the same forwards and backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever direction you take, it is a tale of the bourgeoisie.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA SAGA is a British term for a novel of comfortable rural middle-class life, named after the Aga cooking range.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre label describes novels about well-off English families in country kitchens, a bourgeois tale.

clue.text: Shame the FT's going after attractive person working

indicators.note: going after places the newspaper's possessive at the end, following the other pieces

parts.note: a dish is slang for a good-looking person
a machine that is working is on
the setter writes for the FT, so the paper's own belongings are ours

explanation.surface: Disgrace for the newspaper chasing a good-looking employee.
explanation.walkthrough: FT setters refer to the paper as 'we', so 'the FT's' gives the possessive ours, short form; 'going after' places it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonour is disgrace or loss of reputation, a state of humiliation.

clue.text: Chemist's first to enter negotiation to supply drugs

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one letter is placed within the longer word

parts.note: mediation is negotiation carried out through a third party

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A pharmacist's leading role in talks to provide medicines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives C from Chemist's, which 'to enter' puts inside MEDIATION; 'to supply' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Medication is the general term for medicines or pharmaceutical remedies.

clue.text: Cricket ground of no value

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters are drawn from inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A cricket venue that is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground. The surface reads 'of no value' as worthless, but the letters run across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval in south London is a famous Test match venue, a cricket stadium.

clue.text: Fake empty promises due to be rejected

indicators.note: an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters
rejected means turned back, so the word due is read backwards

explanation.surface: Hollow pledges owed are thrown out as phoney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves PS from promises; 'to be rejected' turns DUE into EUD.
explanation.definitionFit: A pseud is a pretentious poser, someone affected or phoney.

clue.text: Providing coverage about film's finale is spoiling

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the longer word goes round the single letter

parts.note: papering a wall is providing it with a covering

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Giving reviews of a movie's ending ruins it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finale' gives M from film's, which PAPERING goes 'about'; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pampering means indulging someone excessively, which is spoiling them.

clue.text: Incomplete picture that may indicate a fever

definitions.meaning: a photograph showing only the face and shoulders, not the whole body
read as a phrase, the cranium has a high temperature

explanation.definitionFit: A portrait of only the face is a partial photograph; a hot forehead is a sign of feverish illness.

clue.text: Possibly does run away when captured by soldiers

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the soldiers surround the other piece

parts.note: soldier ants are a caste of ant, so ants can stand for soldiers
to elope is to run away to marry

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone flees when troops take them prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe, female deer; 'captured by' is the container signal and 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are deer-like grazing animals, and does are female deer, so the question mark-like 'Possibly' marks an example.

clue.text: Little boy swallows fly

indicators.note: swallows means takes inside, so the boy surrounds the insect

parts.note: a son is a boy child
a midge is a tiny flying insect

explanation.surface: A small child gulps down an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' looks like an adjective describing the boy, but it is the definition, a noun meaning a tiny amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a very small amount, a tiny bit.

clue.text: One stretches to live longer, say

indicators.note: say means spoken out loud, so the phrase is matched by its sound

parts.note: living longer means one will die later

explanation.surface: Someone does exercises in order to extend their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' asks you to speak DIE LATER, which sounds like the medical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilator is a device or muscle that widens or expands an opening.

clue.text: Laconic part for Peter Sellers

indicators.note: part means a portion, so the letters lie within the actor's name

explanation.surface: A clipped role written for the comic actor Peter Sellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part' signals the letters inside peTER SEllers; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic speech is brief and to the point, using few words.

clue.text: See 5
Like a good polka dress to be sharply observed

definitions.meaning: a polka-dot frock is covered in dots, plentifully dotted
noticed with keen eyes, as in praise for an astute observation

explanation.definitionFit: A dotted dress is generously patterned with dots; a keen-eyed observation earns praise for noticing.

clue.text: Rotund feature cheers on articulation?

definitions.meaning: a fold of fat under the jaw on a plump person
the spoken toast chin-chin, which is the word chin said twice

explanation.definitionFit: Plump people often have a fold below the jaw; the toast chin-chin repeats one word, a doubled jaw-word.

clue.text: See 3
Thoughts of cycling aside

indicators.note: cycling means moving letters round from one end to the other

explanation.surface: Musings on riding a bike, set to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' moves AS from the front of ASIDE to the back; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are notions or concepts formed in the mind.

clue.text: Content from Cairo, etc, aimed for transmission

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Material from Egypt's capital and elsewhere intended for broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content from' gives AIR, T and IME; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Airtime is the period during which a programme or advert is broadcast.

clue.text: See 20
Tawdry decoration lacking essence

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter, which is taken away here

parts.note: a garnish is a decoration on food

explanation.surface: Cheap ornament with no real substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking essence' removes N, the middle of the seven letters of GARNISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish means showy and gaudy, much like tawdry.

clue.text: Book for charity to follow as an afterthought

indicators.note: to follow places the charity after the afterthought

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a note added as an afterthought
alms are charitable gifts to the poor

explanation.surface: A volume for good causes comes along as a last-minute addition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' signals that the charity comes after the afterthought; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Psalms is a book of the Old Testament, a biblical collection of hymns.
